design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated to either the walking exercise group or usual care control group, with central randomization stratified by NYHA class.

domain_judgments.rationale: Central stratified randomization with concealed allocation sequence was used, and baseline characteristics were well-balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization was stratified by NYHA class. Allocation concealment was ensured by central randomization and nominal communication of patient allocation in the two arms of the study across the whole recruitment phase of the trial.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although patients were unblinded due to the behavioral nature of the exercise intervention, an intention-to-treat analysis approach was applied and there is no indication of unplanned deviations from the protocol that biased the effect of assignment to intervention.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We used intention-to-treat analyses for both the primary study outcomes (the 6MWT and the 5STS), as well as for hospitalizations. Missing longitudinal 6MWT and 5STS data were imputed along with recommendations made for the analysis of longitudinal data.

domain_judgments.rationale: There was an overall attrition rate of 23% with differential dropout between the exercise arm (31% dropout, 47/151) and the control arm (15% dropout, 22/145), and while missing longitudinal data were imputed, missingness could plausibly be related to participants' functional status.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: 227 of 296 patients (77%) could be retested after 6 months (104 in the active arm [hemodialysis, =90; CAPD, =14] and 123 in the control arm [hemodialysis, =102; CAPD, =21]).

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome assessors conducting the functional capacity tests (6MWT and 5STS) were not blinded to intervention assignment, which introduces potential risk of bias for effort-dependent physical performance measures despite standardized testing rules.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Even though members of this team were extraneous to the daily management of patients on hemodialysis and were in contact with patients and nurses only during the initial training and in the testing sessions, no special measure was adopted to keep them blind to patient allocation. No encouragement was allowed during the testing sessions.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered (NCT01255969), and the reported primary and secondary outcomes correspond with the pre-specified protocol and analytical methods.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The protocol of the EXCITE trial (Clinicaltrials.gov identifier: NCT01255969) was approved by the hospital ethics committees... The primary outcome of the EXCITE study was functional capacity changes (from baseline to 6 months) assessed by the 6MWT and the 5STS, induced by the home-based exercise program and changes in quality of life as measured by the KDQOL-SF.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns due to differential loss to follow-up between study arms (domain 3) and lack of blinding among assessors measuring effort-dependent physical performance outcomes (domain 4).

design_rationale: The authors state that participants 'were divided randomly into a test group and a control group using a computerized random number generator.'

domain_judgments.rationale: Although a computerized random number generator was used, there is no mention of allocation concealment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients fulfilling the inclusion criteria were divided randomly into a test group and a control group using a computerized random number generator.

domain_judgments.rationale: Blinding of participants and personnel was not possible due to the nature of the exercise intervention, and the analysis was a complete-case analysis rather than intention-to-treat, though adherence/deviations were not reported to cause substantial concern.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Four patients were withdrawn from the study: in the test group one patient underwent a kidney transplant and one patient was transferred to another hospital for haemodialysis treatment; in the control group one patient was unwilling to continue and one patient died from an unrelated cause (Figure 1). Therefore, 65 patients completed the whole study, giving a completion rate of 94.2%...

domain_judgments.rationale: Loss to follow-up was low (5.8% overall) and balanced between groups (2 out of 34 vs 2 out of 35) with reasons documented.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Therefore, 65 patients completed the whole study, giving a completion rate of 94.2% and drop-out rates in the test and control groups of 5.9% and 5.7%, respectively.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes include subjective self-reported quality of life (KDQOL-SF) and effort-dependent physical functional tests assessed by unblinded staff in unblinded participants, which could be influenced by knowledge of group assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The questionnaire was completed by the patients themselves under the guidance of the research staf at the start of the study and after 12 weeks.

domain_judgments.rationale: There is no mention of a pre-registered trial protocol or pre-specified statistical analysis plan to rule out selective reporting across multiple functional measures and questionnaire subscales.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary monitoring indicators (exercise capacity and the kidney disease quality of life score [KDQOL-SF; www.rand.org) were measured in both groups at the begin ning of the study and after 12 weeks.

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is high due to the high risk in measurement of the outcome, where unblinded participants self-reported quality of life and completed effort-dependent physical tests under unblinded staff guidance, combined with some concerns regarding allocation concealment and lack of pre-registration.

design_rationale: The study is explicitly described as a randomized 2 x 2 factorial trial where 79 participants were randomly assigned to four treatment groups by a research pharmacist using variable block sizes.

domain_judgments.rationale: Random sequence generation using variable block sizes was conducted by a research pharmacist and allocation concealment was preserved until assignment, with no major baseline imbalances observed.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants were randomly assigned to treatment groups in a 1:1:1:1 manner by the research pharmacist using variable block sizes, which were not known to investigators until the completion of the study. Investigators received a package with 12 vials of study drug or placebo and a card with exercise group assignment from the pharmacy after each participant was assigned.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although the pharmacological intervention was double-blinded, the exercise training intervention could not be blinded to participants and trial personnel, and an available-case modified intention-to-treat approach was used without full description of potential deviations or their impact on self-reported and physical outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: For the analysis of outcomes, all available data were analyzed according to the original treatment assignment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Attrition was relatively low (11 out of 79 patients did not complete, ~14%), balanced across groups, with reasons clearly accounted for and similar across arms.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Sixty-eight patients completed the study. Reasons for noncompletion are shown in Figure 1. Six participants discontinued study drug (four who were receiving placebo and two who were receiving nandrolone) before the end of the treatment period, only two of whom discontinued all study participation. Therefore, results for the four patients who discontinued study drug but were still available for follow-up measures are included in analyses.

domain_judgments.rationale: While objective measures (DEXA, MRI) are unlikely to be influenced by lack of blinding, outcomes also include subjective self-reported measures (SF-36, HAP, POMS) and performance tests where participants and evaluators were aware of exercise assignment and assessor blinding is not described.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Primary outcomes included change in lean body mass (LBM) measured by dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry, quadriceps muscle cross-sectional area measured by magnetic resonance imaging, and knee extensor muscle strength. Secondary outcomes included changes in physical performance, self-reported physical functioning, and physical activity.

domain_judgments.rationale: No clinical trial registry number or published pre-specified statistical analysis plan is provided to confirm that reported outcomes and analyses were pre-specified and free from selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Changes in weight, LBM, and other outcome measures across groups before and after treatment were compared using two-way repeated measures ANOVA with time, exercise, and nandrolone as predictor variables and with the baseline value of the outcome variable as a covariate.

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is judged as 'some concerns' due to the unblinded nature of the exercise intervention affecting subjective and effort-dependent outcomes, absence of explicit assessor blinding for performance tests, and lack of a prospectively registered protocol/statistical analysis plan.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly assigned to the intervention or control group using a computer-generated randomization list.

domain_judgments.rationale: While a computer-generated random sequence was generated, there is no mention of allocation concealment methods (e.g., sequentially numbered opaque sealed envelopes or central allocation).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Eligible patients were randomized into two groups using a computer-generated randomization list.

domain_judgments.rationale: Due to the nature of the exercise intervention, participants could not be blinded, but all randomized participants completed the protocol without reported deviations or dropouts, and analysis adhered to the assigned groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Intervention group patients received 4 training sessions per week, held on non-hemodialysis days for a period of 4 months, whereas control group patients continued their regular lifestyle practice without direct intervention from the personnel of this investigation.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for all 41 randomized participants across all reported outcomes, with zero attrition reported in the flow diagram.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Intervention group consisted of 21 exercising male patients and control group consisted of 20 non-exercising male patients (Table 1)... All 41 allocated participants were followed up and included in the analysis.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome assessors were explicitly blinded to group allocation, and standard, validated physical and biochemical measurement tools were utilized across both groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All assessments were performed by the same experienced investigator who was blinded as to the patients group assignment.

domain_judgments.rationale: There is no mention of a pre-registered trial protocol or pre-specified statistical analysis plan to verify that outcomes and analyses were selected prior to unblinding.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Data were analyzed using a mixed measures (group × period) analysis of variance (ANOVA) for repeated measures.

overall_summary: The study is judged to have some concerns overall due to the lack of information regarding allocation sequence concealment (Domain 1) and the absence of a prospective clinical trial registration or analysis plan (Domain 5).

design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated to either the exercise training group or the control group using a coin flip.
overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is rated as high primarily due to substantial missing outcome data (31% dropout rate) evaluated via a completers-only analysis without ITT. Lack of allocation concealment and blinding of outcome assessors also contribute to the risk of bias.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly assigned to the two intervention groups in a 1:1 ratio using customized randomization software.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although allocation was generated using customized randomization software and groups were balanced at baseline, there is insufficient detail regarding allocation concealment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The randomization procedure was completed using customized randomization software. After the randomization procedure, patients were asked to change their HD day or shift (morning or afternoon session) in order to match with the intervention arm in which they were randomized.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study employed a sham/control exercise intervention to maintain blinding, all participants completed the assigned protocol, and no deviations from intended intervention were reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The patients of both groups exercised under the supervision of an exercise physiologist, during different dialysis days in order to sustain the single-blind design. ... All patients completed the exercise programme with no adverse effects.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for all 24 randomized participants at 6 months with zero dropouts.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All of the patients successfully completed the 6-month intervention programme with no adverse effects and no augmentation phenomena to report.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome measures were standard validated instruments administered under a single-blind design with identical timing and conditions across groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The severity of RLS symptoms was evaluated using the IRLSSG severity scale, functional capacity by a battery of tests, while sleep quality, depression levels and daily sleepiness status were assessed via validated questionnaires, before and after the intervention period. ... The patients of both groups exercised under the supervision of an exercise physiologist, during different dialysis days in order to sustain the single-blind design. In order to avoid any potential acute effects of exercise on the examined variables (RLS severity), all assessments performed 48 h after the last exercise session.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study was registered prospectively (NCT00942253) and reports predefined primary and secondary outcomes according to the planned analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Clinical Trial Registry number. NCT00942253.

overall_summary: The trial is at some concerns overall due to lack of explicit information regarding allocation concealment during the randomization process, despite low risk across all other domains.

design_rationale: The study states that participants were randomly assigned to either the aquatic exercise program or control group using simple allocation (drawing lots).

domain_judgments.rationale: While drawing lots is a random allocation mechanism, there is no mention of allocation concealment, raising some concerns.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: They were randomly assigned by simple allocation (drawing lots) to either a 4-month therapeutic aquatic exercise program (Group A-15 patients), or control status (Group B- 12 patients).

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants were aware of their intervention assignment due to the nature of the exercise intervention, and two dropouts were excluded without clear indication of an intention-to-treat analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In Group a fifteen subjects (thirteen male) completed all phases of assessment and intervention. In Group B twelve subjects (eleven male) were also assessed, at the beginning and at the end of four months. Two patients dropped out of the study due to lack of interest and for personal reasons (family health issues).

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for 27 of 29 participants (over 93%), making the proportion of missing data small and unlikely to bias results substantially.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 93.1% of participants (27 patients) completed all exercise sessions (Figure 1)... Two patients dropped out of the study due to lack of interest and for personal reasons (family health issues).

domain_judgments.rationale: There is no mention of blinding of outcome assessors for physical performance tests, and self-reported quality of life (SF-36) is vulnerable to participant awareness of intervention assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All participants also completed SF-36 Questionnaire... Six Minute Walk tests, Sit to Stand test, Sit and Reach test, Handgrip test, Timed Up and Go test were evaluated.

domain_judgments.rationale: There is no mention of a pre-registered trial protocol or pre-specified statistical analysis plan to verify whether results were reported without selective outcome reporting.

overall_summary: The study has some concerns overall due to lack of reported allocation concealment, lack of assessor blinding for performance and subjective outcomes, and the absence of a pre-registered trial protocol or pre-specified analysis plan.
